NutriFresh Foods - Q2 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriFresh Foods Q2 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the question-and-answer session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriFresh Foods' Q2 results. Joining me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and David Kim, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q2 FY2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue, organic revenue growth overall and by region, impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue, and discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies.

First, regarding e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue: Our digital channels posted impressive gains, with sales surging over 50% year-over-year and now representing nearly one-fifth of total revenue, outpacing industry benchmarks.

Second, concerning organic revenue growth overall and by region: We achieved solid mid-single-digit growth on an organic basis, fueled by volume and pricing across our major markets, marking continued momentum in our branded portfolio.

Third, in terms of impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: Currency fluctuations created a notable headwind to reported figures, but our underlying business remained robust when adjusted for these effects.

Finally, looking at discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: Targeted price adjustments and optimized mix shifts were key to protecting margins and driving top-line expansion amid cost pressures.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q2 FY2024. Net sales were $1.58 billion, representing an 8% increase year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 42.5%, impacted positively by pricing discipline and productivity gains that more than offset lingering commodity inflation in areas like cocoa and sugar. Operating income reached $260 million, up 12% from last year, and diluted earnings per share were $1.25. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through our quarterly dividend, which we increased by 10% this year, and an ongoing share repurchase program authorizing up to $500 million.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales growth of 7-9%, organic growth of 7-8%, and adjusted EPS of $5.00 to $5.20.

To give everyone deeper insight into the strategic drivers behind these results, let me expand on the four key areas Sarah highlighted, starting with our e-commerce momentum.

E-commerce has been a cornerstone of our digital transformation, and we're thrilled with the robust outcomes that highlight our leadership in the food and beverage industry's move to omnichannel models. In Q2, e-commerce sales hit $285 million, reflecting a 52% year-over-year jump and a 14% sequential increase from Q1. This now accounts for 18% of our total net revenue of $1.58 billion, compared to 12% in the prior-year quarter and 16% last period. That's well ahead of the F&B sector's typical 10-12% digital penetration, per NielsenIQ data, and surpasses competitors such as Mondelez at around 14% or Campbell Soup near 11%.

The surge stems from two main pillars. Direct-to-consumer platforms made up 42% of e-comm sales, rising from 35% a year ago, powered by our NutriFresh Direct app and site. Average order values rose 22% to $68, thanks to tailored bundling via Adobe Experience Cloud and our proprietary AI-driven recommendations, akin to PepsiCo's approach on Snacks.com. Subscription streams, inspired by recurring models like Blue Apron's, expanded 78% to $45 million, with churn under 8% and customer lifetime value exceeding $450 per user.

Marketplace and quick-commerce alliances drove the remaining 58%, with 61% growth from tighter ties to Amazon Fresh, Instacart, and DoorDash, now covering 85% of U.S. metro areas. Same-day options through DoorDash Drive lifted conversion rates 28% in cities, where impulse purchases of our NutriPulse energy bars and HydroBoost functional drinks are booming with wellness demand.

Geographically, the U.S. dominated at $210 million or 74% of e-comm, up 55% on Gen Z and millennial affinity for sustainable plant-based options like OatFlex ready-to-drink oats. APAC delivered $42 million, a 110% increase, via Tmall and Flipkart in China and India, with climate-adapted packaging for ZestTea kombuchas overcoming hurdles that challenged brands like Keurig Dr Pepper. Europe contributed $33 million with 22% growth, tempered by GDPR, but our Ocado pilot in the UK sped fulfillment 35%.

We've committed $25 million year-to-date to infrastructure, shifting to Shopify Plus for DTC scale, SAP Commerce Cloud for inventory across 15 distribution centers, and Google Cloud ML for dynamic pricing, boosting e-comm gross margins 15% to 42.5%. Customer acquisition costs dropped 19% to $12.50, lifting LTV/CAC to 36x, supported by TikTok Shop and Instagram Reels campaigns for SnackSavvy packs that added 3.2 million users.

Beyond growth, e-comm bolsters P&L durability against inflation. As private labels from Aldi and Lidl erode traditional retail share by 2-3% per IRI, our 48% DTC margins—versus 32% blended—added 120 basis points to EBITDA this quarter. It also fuels new product development: 60% of Q3 launches, including low-sugar HydroBoost Zero, were tested via platform A/B trials.

Forward, we project Q3 e-comm at $320-340 million, aiming for 22% of revenue by fiscal year-end 2024 and 30% by 2026, tracking McKinsey's 25% CAGR outlook. This leverages $50 million in 'Digital Harvest' investments, like AR previews for meal kits and blockchain for clean-label transparency, vital as 68% of shoppers seek it per Kantar.

Shifting to organic revenue growth, overall and by region: We posted 7.8% organic growth year-over-year on a constant currency basis in Q2, our ninth straight quarter of gains, exceeding our 4-6% long-term CAGR goal through FY2027. Excluding our Brazil private label dairy divestiture and APAC FX benefits, this showcases the resilience of our core brands in snacks, beverages, and plant-based categories.

This blended 4.2% volume expansion and 3.5% price/mix benefit. Pricing averaged 5-7% regionally to counter input inflation—cocoa up 12%, sugar 8%, palm oil 15% year-to-date per Bloomberg. Premiumization lifted mix, with high-margin stars like NutriGlow functional beverages and HarvestRoot plant-based snacks up 15% in velocity per Nielsen IRI. We captured 110 basis points of share in the $450 billion global F&B space, ahead of Mondelez and PepsiCo in select areas.

By region, across our four main markets comprising 92% of revenue:

North America (45% of total; +9.2% organic): Led by health trends, volumes rose 5.8% via 'Clean Label Revolution' launches like zero-sugar NutriGlow electrolytes and organic HarvestRoot veggie chips in 2,500 Walmart/Kroger stores, with triple-digit distribution jumps. Pricing at +3.4% stayed measured to grow household penetration to 68% per Circana. E-comm hit 22% of NA sales via Amazon/Instacart. Quick-service softness was offset by 7-Eleven C-store wins.

EMEA (28%; +6.1% organic): Moderated by macro in Germany/UK (1.2% income growth per Eurostat), but volumes grew 3.9% on sustainability plays like HarvestRoot 'Carbon Neutral' snacks under EU Green Deal, grabbing 4% savory share. Pricing/mix +2.1% on premium RTD teas amid 10% herb costs. Gains from Carrefour/Tesco expansion and Danone co-manufacturing added €45 million annualized. Q4 'Health Horizon' targets Gen Z on TikTok.

APAC (17%; +8.9% organic): Accelerated on China/SEA urbanization, volumes +6.7% with NutriGlow kombucha/low-cal up 28% on Tmall/Shopee. Pricing +2.1%, mix from 35% Japan premium exports. Vietnam plant added 20% aseptic capacity, cutting lead times 15% for monsoons. Now 25% of global organic lift.

Latin America (12%; +4.5% organic): Steady amid 8% Brazil/Argentina inflation, volumes +2.8% led by Mexico beverages via PepsiCo, +1.5 share per Kantar. Conservative +1.6% pricing for OXXO mass channels (55% penetration). Regenerative cocoa farming saved 7% costs, prepping Q4 holidays.

For FY2024, we see 7-8% organic, Q4 at 8-9% on NPD and easing inputs (cocoa futures -5%). 'Flavor Forward 2025' ramps precision fermentation for 20% innovation revenue by FY2026, outpacing 3.5% global growth per McKinsey.

Next, the impact of foreign exchange rates on revenue: With 55% of revenues from outside North America—via brands like PureSpring sparkling waters, NutriZest juices, and VitalGlow energy shots—USD strength created volatility. Reported net revenues hit $1.58 billion, +5% year-over-year, but constant currency organic growth was 8.1% (5% volume, 2.5% pricing, 0.6% mix to premium like low-sugar PureSpring Zero). FX headwind: $110 million or 3.7 percentage points, up from Q1's 2.4 points.

Regionally: Latin America (18% revenues) saw 320 bps drag—BRL -12% QoQ, MXN -8%, muting Brazil AquaZest promotions (7% local volume) and Argentina pricing (12% constant growth). APAC (22%) -450 bps: INR -6%, CNY -4%, trimming India VitalGlow (11% constant, +9% volume) and Indonesia tea to reported 6.5%; AUD offset slightly. Europe (15%) -250 bps on EUR -5%, softening PureSpring (6% constant to 3.5% reported).

Year-to-date FX headwind $290 million or 3.1 points. Like Coca-Cola's 5-point gap or PepsiCo's 7-point international drag.

Mitigations: Hedge 65-75% translational exposure (USD/EUR 1.08 locked vs. 1.05 spot; USD/BRL 5.20 vs. 5.45; USD/MXN 17.50 vs. 17.80), capping FY downside at $100-150 million. Transactional: 85% local sourcing (PET in Mexico, sugar Brazil), down 20% exposure since 2021.

Strategies: 'Glocal' innovation (halal VitalGlow in Middle East +15%), $200 million Vietnam plant Q1 2024; premium pricing (3-5% EM without volume loss); divest low-margin (Argentina powders) for high-ROIC plant-based.

FY2024 FX 3-4 point headwind, Q3 similar; 2025 neutral per consensus. Constant outlook +7-9%, on away-from-home, 12% e-comm, recycled packaging.

Finally, our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies: These propelled 6.2% Q2 organic growth, beating 4-6% guide, via 5.1% pricing, flat volume, +1.1% mix—best pricing since 2022 peaks. List prices averaged +4.8% (up from Q2's 3.9%), passing 2.7% COGS inflation (cocoa -15% QoQ post-West Africa issues, sugar flat).

Snacks (Apex Crunch, NutriBar): +6.2% hikes, elasticity <-1.2, net realization +7.1%; trade spend -120 bps to 22% via NielsenIQ AI. Beverages (Apex Hydrate vs. Gatorade/Powerade): +4.5%, value packs vs. private label; +3.8% price-mix on premium RTD wellness (12% IRI growth).

RGM via Apex Analytics (Snowflake/ML on 15B transactions from Kroger/Albertsons/Tesco): +180 bps growth.

- Premiumization: Premium snacks 28% revenue (up YoY), 2x margins; like Nestlé KitKat but health-focused. Divest soups ($250M), acquire APAC kombucha.

- Promo/trade: -25% deep discounts, "Buy 2 Get 1" Apex Hydrate +8% ACV; $50M to Amazon/Instacart.

- Tech: ShelfWatch AI dynamic pricing +15% compliance, +$12M revenue.

Regions: NA (65%) +7.4% (6.8% pricing, CPI 3.1%); EMEA (18%) +4.9% (5.2% pricing vs. HFSS); APAC/LATAM (17%) +3.8% (3.1% pricing, MXN volatility; China energy +2 share).

'Value Above All' targets 5-7% organic to FY25, embedding functional nutrition (22% CAGR protein bev per Euromonitor), 85% recyclable packs; 45-47% margins. Q4 pricing 4-5% +100-150 bps RGM; hedged 70% 2025 cocoa/tariffs.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thanks for the question, John. Inflation remains a challenge, particularly in commodities like cocoa, sugar, and palm oil, which saw double-digit increases earlier this year. However, our pricing discipline—averaging 5% across regions—along with productivity from supply chain efficiencies and mix shifts to premium items, allowed us to expand gross margins. We're passing through costs judiciously based on elasticity models, ensuring we protect volumes while maintaining household penetration. This approach has been effective, as evidenced by our 7.8% organic growth and share gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (Morgan Stanley):
What are your plans for HydroBoost Zero and what is the expected impact of the product?

Lisa Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Great question, Emily. HydroBoost Zero, our low-sugar functional beverage launch, is off to a strong start following e-comm validation. Plans include national rollout to 5,000 additional doors in Q3, leveraging Instacart and DoorDash for quick-commerce trials, plus TikTok campaigns targeting wellness seekers. We expect it to contribute $50 million in incremental revenue this year, with 45% margins, driving 2 points of mix benefit and accelerating our premium beverages to 30% of segment sales by FY2025. Early Nielsen data shows 15% velocity versus category average.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Mike Rodriguez (JPMorgan):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Kim (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, Mike. Disruptions from weather and geopolitics persist, but our network of 15 DCs, Vietnam expansion, and 85% local sourcing have built resilience. We've cut lead times 15% with just-in-time inventory and ML forecasting, while regenerative programs with farmers reduced cocoa costs 7%. For Q3, we're 20% over capacity in aseptic for APAC, mitigating monsoons, and blockchain traceability ensures clean-label claims. This supports 4.2% volume growth without margin erosion.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Laura Bennett with Barclays. Please proceed.

Laura Bennett (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Laura, our FY2024 reaffirmation holds firm: 7-9% sales growth, 7-8% organic, $5.00-5.20 adjusted EPS. Q3 e-comm at $320-340 million, organic 8-9%, pricing 4-5%. FX headwind 3-4 points, but hedging caps it. Tailwinds from NPD ramps, away-from-home recovery, and 12% e-comm penetration offset risks like cocoa volatility. We're positioned for margin expansion to 43% and sustained share gains.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriFresh Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
